column3: The Hebrew explicitly names “the sons of Judah”; BSB says “the tribe of Judah.”
The Hebrew calls the bay a “tongue”; BSB uses “bay.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew ends with direct “your southern border” and a future “will be”; BSB has “their southern border” and “was.”
The Hebrew names the Jordan’s “end” twice and the sea’s “tongue”; BSB has “mouth” and “bay.”
The Hebrew explicitly repeats “the border”; BSB states the movements without repeating that noun.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew first names “the valley of the son of Hinnom” and calls the slope a “shoulder”; BSB has “the Valley of Hinnom” and “slope.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew calls the mountainside a “shoulder”; BSB says “slope.”
The Hebrew explicitly repeats “the border” three times and uses “shoulder” for Ekron’s side; BSB leaves the repeated noun implicit and says “slope.”
The Hebrew has singular “this border”; BSB has plural “These are the boundaries.”
The Hebrew says “according to the mouth of the LORD” and names Joshua in that clause; BSB says “According to the LORD’s command to him” and makes Joshua the named subject of giving.
The Hebrew identifies Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai themselves as the three sons of Anak; BSB inserts “the descendants of” before their names.
The Hebrew says he went up to the inhabitants and explicitly repeats Debir’s name; BSB says he “marched against” them and leaves the former-name clause unnamed.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew does not explicitly repeat Caleb’s name as the giver; BSB names him in that clause.
The Hebrew uses pronouns for the woman and the man and asks “What is to you?”; BSB explicitly names Acsah and Othniel and asks “What do you desire?”
The Hebrew leaves the giver unnamed; BSB explicitly names Caleb.
The Hebrew explicitly names “the sons of Judah”; BSB has “the tribe of Judah.”
